setup.name: Prerequisites, T1-T2 only (nothing is started here)
setup.command: test -x /root/Shepherd/.venv/bin/python && git -C /root/Shepherd status --porcelain docs/probes/ src/ tools/ | tee /dev/stderr | wc -l | grep -qx 0 && tmux -V && git --version && ls /root/Shepherd/src/shepherd/store/migrations/ | wc -l | grep -qx 4
setup.expected: the venv python exists; docs/probes, src and tools are unmodified; tmux and git answer; four migrations are on disk

setup.name: playwright imports AND chromium launches UNDER THE HARNESS ENVIRONMENT
setup.command: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/root/.cache/ms-playwright /root/Shepherd/.venv/bin/python -c "import os, pathlib; from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright; p=sync_playwright().start(); ep=pathlib.Path(p.chromium.executable_path); assert ep.exists(), ep; b=p.chromium.launch(headless=True); b.close(); p.stop(); print('chromium ok at', ep)"
setup.expected: executable_path EXISTS on disk and a real launch/close succeeds. B13: js_syntax_check.py and render_check.py both sit behind importorskip for an undeclared dependency, so a machine without playwright collects and PASSES. r4/P1: the check must run with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pinned, because the harness redirects XDG_CACHE_HOME and HOME and executable_path then resolves without raising to a file that is not there.

setup.name: the live marker is deselected, measured as an integer
setup.command: cd /root/Shepherd && a=$(.venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -q 2>/dev/null | tail -1) && b=$(.venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -q -m live 2>/dev/null | tail -1) && echo "default: $a" && echo "live: $b"
setup.expected: live-marked count EQUALS the deselected count. Marker-based, never path-based: three tests/e2e/ node ids are collected by default on purpose (test_live_lane_typechecks.py says so in its own docstring), so a path scan goes red on three intentional tests.

setup.name: the run root and the short runtime dir are minted by the session fixture
setup.expected: env-plan §4 steps 1-2 run INSIDE the pytest process (tests/qa5/runroot.py): the session scratchpad is shared and holds a registered git worktree of the repo under test, so only $SESSION_SCRATCH/qa5-<pid> is minted and only that is removed. XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is /tmp/shq5-<pid>, whose budget is asserted with the product's own plan_socket.

reset.name: No reset: there is nothing to reset
reset.expected: Ephemeral-everything. Each run mints a new run root, a new database file inside it, a new tmux server and a new browser, and destroys all four. The SESSION scratchpad is never fresh and is never destroyed.

reset.name: Sweep abandoned run roots, by our own pattern only
reset.expected: runroot.sweep() removes $SESSION_SCRATCH/qa5-<pid> and /tmp/shq5-<pid> whose pid is NOT alive, reports each removal, and stops if a survivor's pid is alive (a concurrent run). It never removes an entry it did not name — the rule the macwt worktree exists to teach.

reset.name: Sweep abandoned tmux SESSIONS on our own socket, by name
reset.expected: conftest._sweep_panes(), env-plan §4 step 5, BEFORE the four panes are created. Directories were swept at mint and sessions never were: a run that died between new-session and teardown left shepherd_r5a alive, `new-session -s shepherd_r5a` then exits 1 (measured), and the harness bricked itself until somebody killed the panes by hand. The five owned names are killed one by one and the socket is then asserted EMPTY — a survivor under any other name stops the run rather than being tidied away, because nothing else is entitled to be on shepherd-qa and deleting an entry we did not name is the rule runroot.sweep exists to keep. Proved both ways: a planted shepherd_r5a is reported as `swept ['shepherd_r5a']`, and a planted `a_stranger` raises HarnessBlocked.

seed.name: The n>1 world, P0-P7 and twenty-one sessions
seed.expected: tests/qa5/seed.py, run by the session fixture at §4 step 8. Projects and repos through the product's OWN front door; sessions through Store verbs because the only front door that creates one is spawn_session, which starts a real claude process and is forbidden. Asserted on arrival: eight workspaces, two sharing a name, P1=2 repos and P3=1 on the read path, P4 with exactly one handled and one unhandled running session, P5 attached-only.

healthcheck.name: Readiness is TWO signals, because there is no health endpoint (B1)
healthcheck.expected: (1) controld.start does not return until the control socket's `bound` event is set — a real signal the product itself sets, and the only one purely about liveness; (2) GET /api/fleet answers 200 {ok:true} on a bounded retry loop. A step-2 failure after a clean bind is BLOCKED, an environment verdict, never a product FAIL. No `sleep N` anywhere: every wait is a bounded predicate with a loud failure.

scenarios.name: The harness's own guards — pure, no environment, no service
scenarios.given: Nothing. These checks refuse at construction, which is the point of putting them there
scenarios.when: tests/qa5/test_guards.py runs, marked `pure`, so the session fixture is never requested
scenarios.then: Every refusal this package writes is exercised at least once, and a negative control proves each guard still accepts ordinary work
scenarios.expected: exit 0, 18 passed, and NO environment is brought up. Before this file existed, `grep -rn 'pytest.raises' tests/qa5/` returned nothing: _argv's refusals, _check_name's ':' refusal, _alive's pid floor and sweep's live-pid stop were unreached code in every run — and two of them were WRONG. `"kill-server" in words` waved `kill-serv` through (tmux resolves an unambiguous command-name prefix; measured rc=0 on this host, server gone), and `any(word == "-L")` waved the fused `-Lshepherd` through. The teardown predicate is now IMPORTED from the product (shepherd.runner.tmux_cmd.is_server_teardown), which tests/boundaries/ also reads, so the property cannot drift into three spellings.

observations.how: no tmux server is contacted: _argv raises before any subprocess exists
_alive delivers signal 0, which delivers nothing; a guard against a reboot must not be able to cause one
sweep's live-pid case asserts the directory SURVIVES — a sweep that deleted and then complained would satisfy pytest.raises anyway

scenarios.name: QA round 5 — all 35 scenarios, six waves, ONE process
scenarios.given: The seeded n>1 world on a real controld, a real tmux socket with four owned panes, a real chromium, and the two-client SSE rig proved live at bring-up
scenarios.when: The six waves run in their fixed order in a single pytest process
scenarios.then: Every scenario's API, DB, queue, UI and log observation points hold; teardown verifies itself and the repo is byte-identical
scenarios.expected: exit 0. THE WHOLE PACKAGE IS ONE COMMAND ON PURPOSE: the registry, the stream ring and compose._PLANE are module-global (B10), so exactly one composition may exist per process; and wave 3 consumes the binding wave 1's S0 measured, which lives in the session fixture. Splitting the waves across processes would re-run bring-up per wave AND lose that binding. THE REPORT CAN NOW SAY FAIL: conftest.pytest_runtest_makereport writes a FAIL/BLOCKED row for any test that ended non-passing without recording (and OVERRIDES a row a scenario recorded before dying in teardown), and pytest_sessionfinish emits once and publishes qa5-latest.json ONLY when the record set equals PLANNED_SCENARIOS. Measured before this: 140 run files, FAIL total 0, 47 of them all-green with scenarios: 0, each having overwritten latest. Measured after: every one of the 11 mutation runs produced a run file carrying its FAIL row, and none of them published.

observations.how: tests/qa5/wire.py — every request carries Host and every POST carries Origin, because §13's check runs before the body is read
the in-process Store handle controld.start returned; no SQL is executed by the harness against the database
tests/qa5/rig.py — two raw SSE readers owned by the session fixture; `: open` and `: keep-alive` are comment lines and are counted separately, so 'no frame' stays distinguishable from 'socket alive'
tests/qa5/auditprobe.py — the production RotatingJsonlLog under $XDG_DATA_HOME/shepherd/logs/<AUDIT_PREFIX>/, with the prefix and the root resolved from the product, never spelled
playwright against the SERVED page; console.error and pageerror listeners registered BEFORE the first navigation
tests/qa5/tmuxctl.py — `-L shepherd-qa` as argv[1] on every invocation; there is no kill-server at any blast radius; the user's socket is never named
the run file under .cc10x/qa/<wf>/runs/ carries measurements.record_set {planned, recorded, missing, extra, duplicated, complete}; qa5-latest.json is written only when complete is true

scenarios.name: Re-runnability — the same suite, again, with no manual cleanup
scenarios.given: Run 1 has completed and its teardown has verified itself
scenarios.when: The identical command runs a second time with nothing cleaned up in between
scenarios.then: The same verdict per scenario id, or the difference is a finding
scenarios.expected: exit 0, and the per-scenario verdicts match run 1. One run proves nothing about the second: state collisions, leftover fixtures and port conflicts all hide behind a single run. Freshness here rests on the run root's pid-named uniqueness, not on the session directory being empty — it is shared and it is never empty.

observations.how: port=0 everywhere and read back from Controld.port; no fixed port exists in the harness
a new run root per run, named by pid; the sweep removes abandoned ones whose pid is dead
every setting lives in the deleted store or the deleted environment; autonomy_level is driven 2->3->2 by S26 and the store is deleted at teardown

cleanup.name: Teardown runs inside the session fixture and verifies itself
cleanup.expected: env-plan §9 steps 1-9, in order: pages and contexts, then chromium BY HANDLE (never pkill, never a signal to 0, 1 or -1), then playwright, then the SSE readers (joined, not abandoned), then controld CONDITIONALLY — S29 stops it as its own `When` and controld.stop must not be called twice, and the run report records which branch ran — then the panes one by one BY NAME, then the socket asserted EMPTY. Every step raises on its own failure; the failures are collected and re-raised together so one bad step cannot leak what the later steps would have freed.

cleanup.name: The leak check, seven assertions and not one observation
cleanup.command: cd /root/Shepherd && ! ls -d /tmp/shq5-* 2>/dev/null && tmux -L shepherd-qa list-sessions 2>&1 | grep -q 'no server running' && git status --porcelain src/ tools/ docs/probes/ | wc -l | grep -qx 0 && echo 'no leaks'
cleanup.expected: no /tmp/shq5-*; the shepherd-qa socket has no server; src/, tools/ and the frozen docs/probes/ evidence are byte-identical. The chromium check is scoped to CHILDREN OF THE PYTEST PID, never a machine-wide pgrep: a machine-wide match goes red because the user has a browser open, and a gate that goes red for someone else's work gets turned off. `git worktree list` is compared against the bring-up baseline inside runroot.destroy().
